title: CPU steal + scheduler imbalance: investigation notes and runbook draft
content:
Summary:

Short: On 2025-11-14 we observed a spike in pod evictions and degraded tail latency for GPU-backed model endpoints in us-west-2. Initial triage shows kernel CPU steal events on several GPU nodes coincident with a bursty host-level process (host-agent-upgrade.sh) and the kube-scheduler rebalancing preferences leading to hot node packing. This doc captures the timeline, evidence, temporary mitigations, and a runbook draft for on-call.

Impact:
- Time window: 2025-11-14 03:20 - 03:58 UTC (ongoing small flaps until 04:12)
- Affected: ~18 nodes in gpu-pool-usw2 (g5.12xlarge equiv), 110 model endpoints experienced elevated p95 latency and ~23 OOM or eviction events across pods
- Customer reports: elevated 99th token latency, a few internal retries surfaced as errors
- Severity: Sev2 (service degradation for dedicated customers)

How we detected it:
- Alerts: node-cpu-steal-rate > 5% for 5m (prometheus rule), pod-eviction-rate alert triggered
- Traces: Redwood Console traces showing increased server-side latency for tips-of-tail tokens; error spike in /v1/generate endpoints
- SRE oncall flagged from Slack -> started triage

Timeline (reconstructed):
- 03:19 UTC: automated node-reboot job (host-agent-upgrade.sh) kicked off on a subset of hosts due to a config roll (unrelated change)
- 03:20 UTC: kernel cpu steal fractional jumps from ~0.1% baseline to 6-12% on affected nodes
- 03:22 UTC: kubelet reported pod oom-kill events on GPU nodes; pod restarts begin
- 03:24 UTC: scheduler starts rebalancing: pods prefer packing onto few nodes because of nodeAffinity/taints config for GPU bin-packing optimization -> increased per-node CPU contention
- 03:30 UTC: autoscaler scaled up 4 new nodes, but kube-scheduler did not spread older long-running pods evenly which prolonged the hot-node condition
- 03:35 UTC: temporary mitigation applied (cordon unhealthy host-agent nodes + scale up extra nodes and allow descheduling)
- 03:48 UTC: metrics improving, cpu-steal back down to ~0.5% on most nodes; some residual evictions until 04:12 UTC

Observations / Evidence:
- top / vmstat on node ip-10-0-5-23: STEAL spikes matching eviction times. dmesg shows KWorker scheduling bursts around the same timestamps.
- host-agent-upgrade.sh log: multiple dpkg installs and containerd restarts causing short-lived CPU-bound work on host
- kube-scheduler logs: several Bind calls for high-priority pods targeted same nodes due to PreferredDuringScheduling affinity weight that pushes for GPUs with low allocation count (we had a weight of 100 in the scheduler ext config)
- Pod eviction reasons: OutOfMemoryError and NodePressure (cpu) in kubelet summary
- Alerts correlated to nodes with host-agent job active. Nodes without job did not show STEAL spike.

Root cause hypothesis (working):
1) Host maintenance job (host-agent-upgrade.sh) introduced CPU-bound work on hosts (apt/dpkg, local image pulls, containerd restart) causing kernel steal time on virtualized metal (burstable hypervisor behavior).
2) Scheduler affinity/binding policy (intentional for GPU packing) aggressively packed high-priority GPU pods onto nodes that had the maintenance job, amplifying CPU contention per node.
3) Autoscaler reacted by adding nodes but scheduler bin-packing heuristics kept older pods pinned, so spread did not happen quickly enough.

Immediate mitigations executed (and observed effects):
- cordoned affected nodes to prevent new pods from scheduling (command: kubectl cordon <node>) -> reduced new allocations to hot nodes
- added temporary taint to affected nodes: kubectl taint nodes <node> cpu-steal=high:NoSchedule (effectively prevented lower priority pods from landing)
- scaled up gpu-pool-usw2 by 6 nodes (ASG manual override) -> provided headroom for rescheduling
- killed runaway host-agent process where safe (used systemctl stop host-agent-upgrade) on 4 nodes -> STEAL reduced quickly on those hosts

Result: latency and evictions subsided after cordon+scale+stop-host-job. By 03:48 most metrics trended back but a small number of pods needed manual drain+reschedule.

Runbook draft (for on-call):
- Detection signals:
  - Prometheus: node_cpu_steal_seconds_total rate > 0.05 over 5m for >3 nodes in pool
  - Kubelet eviction events > 3 in 10m within gpu-pool
  - Pod p95 token latency > baseline + 200ms for model endpoints in pool
- Triage steps:
  1) Identify affected nodes: promql -> topk(10, increase(node_cpu_steal_seconds_total[5m])) filtered by cluster/pool label
  2) ssh to one or two nodes (prefer low-risk) and run: top -bi, vmstat 1 10, dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 | grep -i kworker
  3) Check host processes: ps auxf | egrep 'host-agent|apt|dpkg|yum|containerd'
  4) kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> to see local pod distribution
  5) Check scheduler logs for Bind failures or burst binds around the timestamp (kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/kube-scheduler)
- Immediate mitigations (if STEAL confirmed):
  a) cordon nodes with >3% steal to prevent new pods landing
  b) apply taint cpu-steal=high:NoSchedule to temporarily move scheduling decisions away
  c) if host job is known and safe to stop: systemctl stop host-agent-upgrade && pkill -f host-agent-upgrade.sh (careful: check maintenance windows and owners)
  d) if safe, drain and kubeadm delete pod eviction for long-running pods that are misallocated: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
  e) scale up pool if headroom low (manual ASG override) and uncordon after stable
- Post-incident steps for SRE:
  - Add a scheduler policy guard: avoid strong hard-weighted PreferredDuringScheduling for GPU packing when node-level STEAL > threshold
  - Ensure host maintenance jobs are scheduled through k8s jobs with node-level throttling (nice/ionice) or run on maintenance window when autoscaler has buffer
  - Add automation: detect host-agent job and pre-cordon node until work completes or CPU steal goes below 0.5%
  - Work with infra to limit host-side dpkg/apt loops running simultaneously on multiple nodes (stagger)
  - Revisit autoscaler and scheduling interplay: consider auto-descheduling of older pods when new capacity comes up in the same pool

Commands & PromQL handy references:
- Find nodes by steal: topk(10, rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="steal"}[5m]))
- List pods on node: kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node>
- Cordon: kubectl cordon <node>
- Taint: kubectl taint nodes <node> cpu-steal=high:NoSchedule --overwrite
- Drain (use with caution): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did autoscaler add nodes but scheduler did not spread workloads quickly? (need to review scheduler predicates and cluster-autoscaler interaction)
- Is hypervisor-level CPU steal caused by noisy neighbor on host? Or strictly due to host agent process? Need cloud provider VM metrics and hypervisor-level telemetry.
- Do we need a new Prometheus alert specifically for host-agent jobs starting (we can instrument host-agent to emit an event)

Action items and owners:
- Lina: dig into kube-scheduler config & PR to soften PreferredDuringScheduling weight (target by 2025-11-21)
- Marco: add instrumentation and event emission from host-agent (small PR) so we can correlate maintenance windows to STEAL alerts (target 2025-11-25)
- Jon: propose autoscaler tweak to trigger a reschedule window when new nodes are added (RFC 2w)
- Ava: formalize runbook into PagerDuty play and add to SRE runbooks page, include the PromQL queries and commands (target 2025-11-19)

Notes to self / informal: there were a few pods with hostPath local caches that made drain slow; consider "--delete-local-data" but watch for data loss. Also, downstream teams might be surprised if we stop host-agent mid-maintenance — need to coordinate.

References:
- slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234ABC/p1637020192000
- infra PR on host-agent: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789
- incident ticket: INC-2025-1423

End of notes.
